steps.intent: Our objective is to secure a clean twelve-month renewal of the Al-Shabaab sanctions regime, with robust IED-component controls, effective humanitarian exemptions and strong support for AUSSOM and Somali-led security efforts. We expect difficult points to include the duration of the renewal, humanitarian carve-out language and any additional reporting burdens, and we will consult closely with African members and other partners to keep the text consensus-viable and avoid a veto.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of the sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, and appreciates the penholder's inclusive approach. We request two amendments: in OP1, explicitly reaffirm that the arms embargo does not apply to the Federal Government of Somalia, consistent with resolution 2713 (2023); and in OP6, add predictable and sustainable financing for AUSSOM, including through implementation of resolution 2719 (2023), and anchor coordination in full respect for Somalia's sovereignty, territorial integrity and African ownership. These adjustments would align the text with Council decisions and African priorities, and we can support the text with these changes.
messages.China: China supports the draft as currently formulated. It appropriately reaffirms Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, maintains targeted sanctions with humanitarian exemptions, and includes fair and clear listing and delisting procedures. We encourage the penholder to preserve Council unity and ensure the timely renewal of the mandate and Panel of Experts.
messages.Denmark: Denmark fully supports the renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, including the clear humanitarian exemption and fair and clear procedures. Given that the current measures expire today, we urge the Council to adopt the draft promptly without amendment.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime and the Panel mandate, and we thank the United Kingdom for a balanced draft. We ask the penholder to restore the Council’s longstanding reference to the Djibouti-Eritrea border dispute, which France has consistently considered important for regional peace and security. We also seek explicit clarification in OP1 that the arms embargo remains targeted and does not restrict weapons and military equipment destined for the Somali authorities, consistent with prior Council decisions.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the swift renewal of the Somalia sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate and welcomes the draft’s targeted approach and humanitarian exemptions. We would ask the penholder to strengthen the text on the prompt and transparent processing of humanitarian exemptions, and to reflect Greece’s strong interest in counter-piracy and maritime security cooperation, consistent with international law including UNCLOS. We would also welcome language on protection of civilians and respect for international humanitarian and human rights law in security cooperation.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of the Somalia sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate and thanks the penholder for a balanced text. We ask for strengthened reporting on the humanitarian exemption in OP2 and a regular assessment of the measures' humanitarian impact. We also propose that OP6 recognize predictable and sustainable financing for AUSSOM, consistent with Somali ownership and African-led peace support.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports this renewal and welcomes the targeted sanctions and strengthened humanitarian exemption language. We request two small adjustments: add terrorist financing to the PP5 list of threats, and explicitly reaffirm the principle of non-interference in Somalia's internal affairs in PP2. With these changes, Pakistan is ready to support the text.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of the sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate and welcomes the strong humanitarian exemption and fair-and-clear-procedures language. We request one minor addition to OP6 to anchor coordination and support for Somali-led security efforts in international humanitarian law and human rights law and in the protection of civilians. With that small adjustment, Panama is ready to support the text.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current text and commends the penholder for a balanced renewal that maintains the sanctions regime, strengthens humanitarian exemptions, and extends the Panel of Experts. We encourage full implementation by all Member States and coordinated support for AUSSOM and Somali-led security efforts. We look forward to consensus adoption.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate as reflected in the draft. We note that the text already includes targeted measures, humanitarian exemptions, and respect for Somalia’s sovereignty. We therefore see no need for changes and are prepared to vote in favour.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the draft as circulated. We welcome the renewal of targeted measures, the strengthened humanitarian exemption language, and the emphasis on Somali ownership and AUSSOM coordination. We encourage the penholder to maintain this balanced text and to ensure the Committee operates transparently and expedites exemption requests.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the timely renewal of the Somalia sanctions and the Panel mandate and welcomes the clear humanitarian exemption. We ask the penholder to strengthen references to the protection of humanitarian and medical personnel, respect for international humanitarian law, and women's full, equal and meaningful participation. These are important but not red lines; we remain ready to join consensus.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of the sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, and welcomes the draft’s reaffirmation of Somali sovereignty and humanitarian exemptions. We ask the penholder to clarify that the arms embargo does not apply to the Federal Government and its security forces, to recognize the Federal Government’s primary responsibility for security in OP4, and to add a call for predictable and sustainable funding for AUSSOM, including through assessed contributions. These changes are essential for a coherent and Somali-owned security transition.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the draft as presented. It renews the necessary sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate while preserving humanitarian exemptions and maintaining focus on Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia. We encourage all Member States to implement the measures fully, particularly to curb Al-Shabaab’s access to funds, weapons, and IED components.

steps.summary: The revised text renews the Somalia sanctions and Panel mandate through 28 February 2026 while adding consensus humanitarian, IHL, maritime-security, counter-terrorist-financing and Somali-ownership language. It accommodates most Council requests, including AUSSOM financing references via resolution 2719 without explicit assessed contributions, and is expected to be adopted unanimously.

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the partial incorporation of its earlier proposals, especially the clarification of the arms embargo and the reaffirmation of Somalia’s sovereignty and African ownership. We support the renewal of the sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, but we still need OP6 to reflect the full and effective implementation of resolution 2719 (2023), including consideration of UN assessed contributions, so that AUSSOM’s financing is genuinely predictable and sustainable. We are ready to join consensus if this remaining point is addressed.
messages.China: China supports the current draft and commends the penholder for the inclusive consultations. The text reaffirms Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and African ownership, and maintains targeted sanctions with clear humanitarian exemptions and due-process safeguards. We welcome the focus on predictable support for AUSSOM and on humanitarian access. China will vote in favour of the draft.
messages.Denmark: Denmark fully supports the current text and has no further requests. We welcome the strengthened humanitarian exemption and reporting language, the reference to women, peace and security, and the calls for predictable and sustainable AUSSOM financing. We encourage prompt adoption of the resolution.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime and welcomes the targeted-embargo and humanitarian-exemption language. We regret that a separate preambular paragraph on the Djibouti-Eritrea dispute was rejected, but we ask that this concern be reflected by amending PP2 to refer explicitly to that border dispute, consistent with France’s long-standing position. This is important for France’s support and for keeping the Council engaged in unresolved regional disputes.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the current draft and welcomes the incorporation of our proposals on humanitarian exemption transparency, maritime security and UNCLOS, and international humanitarian law and protection of civilians. We encourage the Council to adopt the text promptly and to remain actively engaged on implementation, including through the requested reporting on humanitarian impact.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for incorporating our priorities on humanitarian exemptions, Committee reporting and the Secretary-General’s humanitarian-impact assessment, as well as sustainable AUSSOM financing. The text maintains a targeted sanctions regime, respects Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and supports Somali-led security efforts. Guyana therefore supports the current draft and encourages the Council to adopt it by consensus.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the adoption of the current text. We welcome the incorporation of our earlier proposals on terrorist financing and the principle of non-interference in Somalia’s internal affairs, and we are satisfied that the draft maintains targeted sanctions, clear humanitarian exemptions and fair listing and delisting procedures while respecting Somalia’s sovereignty and African ownership. We encourage the Council to adopt the resolution without further delay.
messages.Panama: Panama welcomes revision 1, particularly the strengthened humanitarian exemption language, the references to international humanitarian law and human rights law, and the protection-of-civilians focus in OP6. We also value the reporting requirement on humanitarian impact and the balanced treatment of Somalia’s sovereignty and AUSSOM financing. Panama can support the draft as it stands and encourages the Council to adopt it promptly before the current measures expire.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current text as a balanced and consensus-oriented renewal. We welcome the strengthened humanitarian exemption language, the extension of the Panel of Experts, and the focus on predictable support for AUSSOM. We have no further changes and encourage the Council to adopt the text.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the current text. It preserves the targeted nature of the sanctions against Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia, reaffirms Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and includes clear humanitarian exemptions and fair listing and delisting procedures. We welcome the emphasis on Somali ownership and African solutions and are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the penholder and supports the revised text as presented. We particularly welcome the retained humanitarian exemption procedures, the targeted sanctions language, and the stronger references to AUSSOM coordination and predictable financing. We are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes revision 1 and the incorporation of our requests on protection of humanitarian and medical personnel, women’s full, equal and meaningful participation, and international humanitarian law and protection of civilians in OP6. The text is balanced, preserves essential humanitarian exemptions and reporting, and supports Somali-led security efforts alongside predictable financing for AUSSOM. We can support the draft as it stands.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the penholder for incorporating OP1 and OP4 and broadly supports the revised text. We continue to stress that AUSSOM requires predictable and sustainable financing; OP6 should explicitly reference United Nations assessed contributions in line with resolution 2719 (2023). This is important for the mission's ability to support Somali-led security efforts.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the draft as circulated. We welcome the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, as well as the balanced humanitarian exemptions and monitoring provisions. We encourage the Council to adopt the text promptly to maintain pressure on Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria’s key requested amendment to OP6 was accepted, and the resolution aligns with its priorities on African ownership, AUSSOM financing, targeted sanctions, and humanitarian safeguards, so it would vote in favour.
reasons.China: China has consistently supported targeted Somalia sanctions renewals with humanitarian safeguards and respect for Somali sovereignty, and it supported this draft in the last negotiation round. There is no basis for China to oppose or veto a balanced renewal.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supported the prior renewal and this draft reflects its priorities on targeted sanctions, humanitarian exemptions, protection of civilians, and Somali-led security. Denmark therefore votes yes and uses a short explanation of vote in support.
reasons.France: France’s key requested language on the Djibouti–Eritrea dispute was accepted, and the draft aligns with its support for targeted sanctions, humanitarian safeguards, and Somali-led security efforts. France therefore votes in favour and explains its vote to reinforce these priorities.
reasons.Greece: Greece consistently supports renewing the Somalia sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate, and the draft includes humanitarian safeguards and support for Somali-led security efforts consistent with Greece’s positions.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana supported the prior renewal and the draft maintains targeted sanctions and humanitarian exemptions; it requested no changes and is likely to vote in favour without speaking before the vote.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan was recorded as supporting the draft in the final negotiation round and made no requests for changes; the text advances counterterrorism cooperation, Somali sovereignty, and humanitarian safeguards consistent with Pakistan’s positions. Therefore Pakistan votes in favour without a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.Panama: Panama supported the prior renewal and the draft’s targeted sanctions, humanitarian exemptions and AUSSOM financing provisions are consistent with its positions. With no requested changes and a straightforward vote in favour, Panama does not need a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supported the previous renewal and remains aligned with the broad Council consensus on countering terrorism and stabilizing Somalia. The draft addresses ROK priorities on sanctions implementation, humanitarian safeguards, and coordinated international support, so a yes vote is consistent.
reasons.Russian Federation: The draft is a routine renewal of targeted Somalia sanctions and the Panel of Experts, maintaining pressure on Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia while preserving humanitarian exemptions. Russia had already signaled support and requested no changes, so it votes in favour without a pre-vote statement.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone previously supported all recent Somalia sanctions resolutions and raised no outstanding concerns in the final negotiation round; the draft advances counter-terrorism, humanitarian safeguards, and Somali-led security efforts, consistent with its foreign policy priorities.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia supported the prior renewal and this draft strengthens humanitarian exemptions and accountability mechanisms while maintaining targeted sanctions; it has no outstanding concerns, so it votes in favour without a pre-vote statement.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supported the prior renewal and the draft advances its core priorities on sovereignty, security transition, humanitarian access and AUSSOM support. Although its preferred language on assessed contributions was only partially reflected, the resolution remains strongly in Somalia’s interest, so Somalia votes yes and explains its financing concern.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom is the penholder and has consistently supported renewing the Somalia sanctions regime, Panel of Experts mandate, and humanitarian safeguards. Voting in favour advances UK policy priorities on countering Al-Shabaab, supporting AUSSOM, and preserving Council unity.
reasons.United States of America: The United States supported the renewal of targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate in prior votes and indicated support for the draft without requesting changes. Voting in favor is consistent with its policy of countering Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia while maintaining humanitarian safeguards.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the penholder for taking into account our proposal in paragraph 6, which strengthens the reference to the full and effective implementation of resolution 2719 (2023), including consideration of United Nations assessed contributions, as appropriate. Predictable and sustainable financing for AUSSOM is essential to support Somali-led and Somali-owned security efforts. We also stress that sanctions must remain targeted and proportionate, with effective and timely humanitarian exemptions, and that the sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity of Somalia must be fully respected. Algeria remains committed to supporting African solutions to African challenges and to the fight against terrorism in Somalia and the region.
before.China: China thanks the penholder for its efforts and supports the renewal of the sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We believe that sanctions should remain targeted and proportionate and must include clear and effective humanitarian exemptions, so as to avoid adversely affecting the timely delivery of humanitarian assistance. The sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Somalia must be respected, and Somalia’s ownership and leadership in its security efforts should be upheld. The international community should provide predictable and sustainable support to AUSSOM and to Somali-led security efforts while avoiding interference in Somalia’s internal affairs. China will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Denmark: Denmark will vote in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of targeted sanctions against Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia, together with a robust humanitarian exemption and strengthened reporting on humanitarian impact. We also underline the importance of predictable financing for AUSSOM, respect for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, protection of civilians, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in peace and security efforts. Denmark remains committed to working with the Council and Somali-led institutions to advance peace and stability in Somalia.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime against Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia, and we particularly welcome the inclusion, at France’s request, of the reference to the border dispute between Djibouti and Eritrea, which ensures that the Council remains actively seized of that situation. The text also preserves essential humanitarian exemptions and supports coordinated international efforts in favour of Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and Somali-led security transition. France reiterates the importance of full compliance with the arms embargo and of predictable support for AUSSOM, including through the implementation of resolution 2719 (2023).
before.Greece: Greece votes in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts, welcome the strengthened humanitarian exemptions and reporting, and underscore the importance of predictable support for AUSSOM, the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, and full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts so that the Council can continue to counter Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia, while ensuring humanitarian exemptions are effective and principled. We also stress the importance of predictable support for AUSSOM and full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, protection of civilians, and compliance with international humanitarian law.
before.Somalia: Somalia votes in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of the sanctions regime with clear humanitarian exemptions, the strengthened focus on protecting civilians and humanitarian personnel, and the support for Somali-led and Somali-owned security efforts. We also appreciate the recognition of AUSSOM and the need for predictable and sustainable financing. At the same time, we reiterate that the financing of AUSSOM must be made more predictable, including through consideration of United Nations assessed contributions as appropriate, so that the mission can effectively support Somalia’s security transition. We stress that all Council action must continue to respect Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia continue to pose a serious threat to peace and security in Somalia and the region, and the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate is essential to sustaining international efforts to degrade that threat. This text also strengthens humanitarian safeguards and makes clear that the sanctions are targeted and proportionate, with timely humanitarian exemptions, and it reaffirms our respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and ownership of its security transition. The United Kingdom thanks Council members for their constructive engagement and urges full implementation of the measures, full compliance by all Member States, the protection of civilians, and safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We also reiterate the importance of predictable and sustainable support for AUSSOM, in line with resolution 2719, as part of a coordinated international effort in support of Somali-led security.

after.Guyana:
Thank you, Mr. President. Guyana voted in favour of this resolution. We welcome the renewal of the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts as part of the Council’s support for peace and security in Somalia. We particularly appreciate the strengthened humanitarian exemptions and reporting requirements, and we stress that sanctions must remain targeted and proportionate and must not impede the timely delivery of humanitarian assistance.

Guyana reaffirms its respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity of Somalia and the principle of non-interference in Somalia’s internal affairs. We support Somali-led and Somali-owned security efforts and the need for predictable and sustainable support for AUSSOM, including in line with resolution 2719 (2023). We call for full compliance with the arms embargo and strengthened regional and international cooperation to counter Al-Shabaab, Islamic State in Somalia, the proliferation of IED components, illicit arms trafficking, terrorist financing, the illegal charcoal trade and piracy.

The protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in peace and security efforts remain essential. Guyana remains committed to working with the Council and Somali institutions in support of peace and stability in Somalia and the region.
after.Pakistan: Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime against Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia, and the extension of the Panel of Experts, as terrorism in Somalia continues to pose a serious threat to regional and international peace and security. At the same time, Pakistan stresses that sanctions must remain targeted, proportionate and time-bound, with clear, effective and timely humanitarian exemptions and fair and transparent listing and delisting procedures. We welcome the strengthened humanitarian safeguards in the text. We also reaffirm the need for full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity, and for Somali ownership of its security transition. Pakistan supports predictable and sustainable financing for AUSSOM, including through consideration of United Nations assessed contributions as appropriate, in line with resolution 2719 (2023), and stresses the importance of African-led solutions. We call on all Member States to comply fully with the sanctions measures and to cooperate with the Committee and the Panel of Experts. Pakistan remains committed to supporting peace, security and stability in Somalia and the region.
after.Panama: Panama welcomes the adoption of this resolution and voted in favour. The renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts is a necessary and proportionate response to the continuing threat posed by Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia to regional and international peace and security. We stress that these measures must remain targeted and proportionate and must include clear, timely and effective humanitarian exemptions, so that they do not hinder the delivery of life-saving assistance to civilians. Panama reaffirms its respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity of Somalia and the principle of non-interference in its internal affairs. We support Somali-led and Somali-owned security efforts and the need for predictable and sustainable support for AUSSOM, including through the implementation of resolution 2719 (2023). The protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, as well as safe and unhindered humanitarian access, must remain central. We also underscore the importance of strengthened international cooperation against illicit arms trafficking, IED components, terrorist financing and piracy, in accordance with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.
